name: LNGS — Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso
notes: Linked map: map:cern, because beamline:cngs (CERN's own beamline, facility_id facility:cern) names site:lngs-hall-c as its far_detector_site_ids target (732 km baseline, 2006-2012 beam operation for OPERA/ICARUS). The CNGS direction line itself is drawn on map:cern, not here, since the beamline entity belongs to CERN's inventory, not LNGS's.

geometry:lngs-hall-a, geometry:lngs-hall-b and geometry:lngs-hall-c intentionally share one derived coordinate (the midpoint of the sourced ~700 m access-zone stretch): no source consulted distinguishes the three halls' order or position within that zone, so the three shapes are identical. A sourced (if coarse) position is available for all three and is more informative than leaving any of the three sites undrawn.

The Pandola 2011 overview (src:geo-euro-ug-pandola-2011) names several LNGS experiments that are not in the Atlas (Gator, MACRO, WArP, LUNA, COBRA, DAMA/Libra, STELLA/GEMPI2); they are therefore not listed as not drawn.

schematics.note: Official site-layout figures ('Planimetria ubicazione esperimenti e set-up Laboratori sotterranei LNGS', 'Vista assonometrica dei Laboratori sotterranei') in the laboratory's own external emergency plan; not georeferenced or copied into this dataset (an institutional PDF), cited as a link only. Would be the best source for a future, hall-differentiated position.
schematics.title: LNGS underground laboratories site plan (Piano di Emergenza Esterna INFN-LNGS 2024, Fig. 25/28/29)

summary.plain: The Gran Sasso National Laboratory in central Italy: three underground halls dug beside the 10-kilometre Gran Sasso motorway tunnel, about six kilometres in from the Assergi end, plus the laboratory's surface offices at Assergi.
summary.technical: One local map for facility:lngs. The A24 Gran Sasso road tunnel (OSM relation 9617984) is drawn as context; the underground laboratory's own position is derived from the official emergency plan's motorway chainage of its entrance/exit doors (km 124.150/123.440 against the tunnel's own km 117.653-127.829), giving a ~700 m sourced zone about 5.8-6.5 km from the Assergi portal. Halls A, B and C are drawn at that zone's midpoint, undifferentiated. The surface External Laboratories / Centro Direzionale complex at Assergi carries both an OSM building footprint and the emergency plan's own surveyed WGS84 coordinate (79.6 m apart, corroborating each other).
